about: And My Life Is Yours is a still of Kratos, the pale, red-tattooed Spartan from God of War, standing on dark rocky ground with his arms flung out wide and his head thrown back mid-shout. In the game he is offering his life and loyalty to Ares in exchange for victory, so the image is used for over-the-top surrender: pledging yourself completely the second someone offers you something you want.
origin: The scene is a cutscene from the original God of War, released on PlayStation 2 in 2005: Kratos, about to be cut down by barbarians, begs the god of war to wipe out his foes and offers him eternal service in return.
usage:
Top box: the offer or the deal on the table. Bottom box: the pledge, usually some form of "and my life is yours".

It works for anything you would sell your soul for in the moment: free pizza, a day off, a fix for your bug, a ticket to a sold-out show. The smaller the reward and the bigger the pledge, the better the joke.
ideas: give me one more day on the deadline
the ref giving us a penalty
the barista spelling my name right
aka: Destroy My Enemies and My Life Is Yours
